cards.explanation: The answer is livestock and silver and gold. Genesis 13:2 says Abram had become extremely wealthy in livestock and silver and gold. Three things, and he's loaded with every one. I started out with a 25 cent price sticker on me, friends, so I'm taking notes.

The answer is True! Genesis 13:4 says Abram called on the name of the LORD there, at the site where he had built the altar. He had built that altar earlier, between Bethel and Ai (Genesis 12:8). Now he's back at the same spot, calling on the LORD again. I love that.

The answer is False. Genesis 13:6 says the land was unable to support both of them while they stayed together, for they had so many possessions. They were unable to coexist. Two men with that much stuff, and together it just didn't work.

The answer is Lot. Genesis 13:7 says there was discord between the herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of Lot. Lot is the one who was traveling with Abram (Genesis 13:5). I think the herdsmen were stuck in the middle of this one.

The answer is kinsmen! Abram says it plainly: "After all, we are kinsmen." (Genesis 13:8) He wants no contention between him and Lot, or between their herdsmen. I think that's wise. Some arguments cost way more than they're worth.

The answer is to the right! Abram says, "If you go to the left, I will go to the right; if you go to the right, I will go to the left." (Genesis 13:9) He offers to take the opposite direction from whatever Lot picks. Lot gets to choose first. That's a generous offer.

The answer is that the plain is well watered. Genesis 13:10 says Lot saw that the whole plain of the Jordan, all the way to Zoar, was well watered. For people with huge herds, that's a big deal. Water is how you keep a lot of animals going.

The answer is the land of Egypt! Genesis 13:10 says the plain was well watered like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt. Abram and Lot had just come from there, so they knew it. That's a pretty big compliment for a stretch of land.

The answer is False. The writer adds, "This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah." (Genesis 13:10) So the destruction hasn't happened yet when Lot looks out. It's a little heads-up from the writer, and I'll leave it right there.

The answer is EAST! Genesis 13:11 says Lot chose the whole plain of the Jordan for himself and set out toward the east. The WHOLE plain, friends. He didn't pick a corner, he picked it all. Then the verse says Abram and Lot parted company.

The answer is True, and it's a serious line. Genesis 13:13 says the men of Sodom were wicked, sinning greatly against the LORD. Lot pitched his tent toward that city (Genesis 13:12). The writer just says it plainly and moves on.

The answer is offspring! The LORD says, "…for all the land that you see, I will give to you and your offspring forever." (Genesis 13:15) It's a promise for Abram and for those who come after him. That's a long gift.

The answer is an altar to the LORD! Genesis 13:18 says Abram built it at Hebron, near the Oaks of Mamre. He had built an altar earlier between Bethel and Ai (Genesis 12:8). Now there's a new one by his new home.
